decisions.reason: This flagship reference electrometer sits close to the core dosimetry business and is still featured on the home page, so it costs little to carry and its value is being realized.

The oncology risk management software builds on the established offer and still has its own page; as a low-cost software option with unresolved but plausible value for QA convergence, it is worth keeping.
The CT phantom was launched only recently, fits the imaging QA direction, and has little carrying cost, so the option should stay open while uncertainty resolves.
Although distant from the core and one of several overlapping mammography options, it was launched just in 2024, so its uncertainty has not yet resolved and keeping it is cheap.

This second mammography phantom overlaps with Product D and is distant from the core, which makes it a candidate for consolidation; it is too early to conclude its value will not be realized, so it stays for now.
